newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia Suharto's daughter denies family dynasty.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia Suharto's daughter denies family dynasty.

text.p: The eldest daughter of 75-year-old Indonesian President Suharto has strongly denied the existence of a family dynasty, the Republika newspaper reported on Sunday.
"There is no Suharto dynasty," Siti Hardiyanti Rukmana, one of seven chairmen of the Golkar party, told reporters while campaigning in East Java on Saturday.
Rukmana, a high profile figure in the ruling Golkar campaign, has often been mentioned during recent media speculation as a possible candidate for vice-president.
Two brothers Bambang Trihatmodjo and Hutomo Mandala Putra and one sister Siti Hediati Hariyadi, who like Rukmana are all prominent businesspeople, are also high profile figures in Golkar.
"Opinions like that are absolutely not true," Rukmana, commonly known as Tutut, said repeatedly.
"The Suharto family does not need to be chosen as president or vice-president," Rukmana, head of the Citra Lamtoro Gung Persada group, said.

In March next year, the People's Consultative Assembly (MPR) is expected to elect Suharto to his seventh five-year term as president. The body, half of whose members the president himself chooses, has elected Suharto unopposed six times.
Despite recent public reflections on his age and concerns about his health, Suharto is widely expected to run again for a seventh term.
